title: A watcher-driven ingest silently reverts a completed store write when the on-disk extract lags
body:
With `intentd` running, a COMPLETED store write can be silently reverted when the on-disk canon extract still holds the pre-write state and the watcher ingests that stale extract back into the store. Observed on ST0064 AC-01.5, 2026-09-01. No client, no error, no attribution -- the write simply is not there a few minutes later.

## Reproduction (measured this session; directly-observed facts kept apart from the inferred mechanism)

DIRECTLY OBSERVED:

- Run 1: `intent ac satisfy ST0064 AC-01.5 --evidence "..."` -> `ok: AC-01.5 satisfied by evidence`, rc=0. `intent ac gate ST0064` -> `5/9 satisfied` (store, read live, 01.5 NOT in the unsatisfied set). Committed the regenerated extract as `5deb477c`.
- Minutes later: `intent ac list ST0064` -> `AC-01.5 satisfied: no`; `intent ac gate ST0064` -> `4/9`; `git show 5deb477c:intent/.canon/st/ST0064.json` reads `.state.is = "unsatisfied"` for AC-01.5. The store had reverted, and the committed extract was unsatisfied.
- Run 2: `intent ac satisfy ST0064 AC-01.5 --evidence "..."` -> ok. THIS TIME verified the DISK extract before committing: `jq '.criteria[]|select(...01.5)|.state.is' intent/.canon/st/ST0064.json` -> `satisfied`. Committed `e8ff6486`. Post-verify: committed extract, `ac list`, and gate all read satisfied, and ST0064.json was NOT re-dirtied.

## The window -- why it hides behind a hundred successful `ac satisfy` calls

It fires only when DISK != STORE at ingest time. Run 2 did not revert because disk == store, so the watcher's ingest was a no-op. A WINDOW, not a constant. Inside the window the two surfaces disagree: `ac list` / gate (store) read satisfied while the on-disk extract read unsatisfied -- and the thing that gets committed and outlives the session is the disk. That disagreement is the observation that makes the mechanism legible rather than mysterious.

## The cure (transferable past this verb)

Verify the DISK extract (`jq .state.is` on `intent/.canon/st/<ST>.json`), not the store or the gate, BEFORE committing a canon write. The store read tells you the write happened; only the disk read tells you what the commit will carry and what the watcher will not undo. This generalises to `at green`, `wp done`, and anything that writes the store while `intentd` watches the disk -- every node here has been verifying the store, which is the wrong surface.

## Mechanism / home (both citations verified in-tree; note there are TWO `store.rs`, one per crate)

THE TRIGGER -- `intentd/src/watch.rs:1-2`: "AC-08.5: debounced, gitignore-aware watching that drives ingest on external edits." `watch.rs:64`: "Start watching a project, driving ingest through its store handle." Started by `intentd/src/registry.rs` via `watch::start` on project open (a project the daemon answers for is one it watches). So a change to the on-disk extract -- including a stale one -- triggers an ingest.

WHY IT IS SILENT, BY DESIGN -- `crates/intentd/src/store.rs:56-70`: "A client request is counted, answered and attributable; a watcher-driven ingest has no client, nobody to answer, and must NOT move `ProjectHandle::dispatched` ... THE SEPARATION IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN A BRANCH. The count lives in `ProjectHandle::call`, which is the client door; the watcher reaches `ProjectHandle::ingest`, which is a different door and cannot increment anything." So the reverting write is UNATTRIBUTABLE BY CONSTRUCTION -- no client, nobody to answer, deliberately outside the op counter (for a good reason: the counter is the `AC-08.2` conformance discriminator, and a background ingest landing inside a harness bracket would report `+2` for one verb). This is the difference between "the daemon sometimes clobbers" and "nothing in the system CAN record who did it, on purpose" -- it is why the loss is silent rather than merely rare.

(The `watch.rs` trigger and the `intentd/store.rs` designed-silence are complementary and both load-bearing. Do NOT confuse `crates/intentd/src/store.rs` with `crates/intentsvcs/src/store.rs:59-67`, which is a different file -- the `written_at`/D39 region -- and is not this citation; the basename is shared across two crates.)

## Family: third member of silent-write-loss-on-canon

- `0210` blocks a commit -- LOUD (the canon-commit guard refuses; the victim at least knows).
- `0206` is two concurrent CLI sessions overwriting each other's canon write (read-modify-write with no compare-and-swap).
- THIS one silently reverts a COMPLETED write, with no client and nobody to attribute it to -- the quietest of the three. All three are silent write-loss on canon.

## Correcting the initial diagnosis

This was first read (by vc, and plausibly by anyone) as operator error -- that the command was never run, or its result never read. It was a race in the tool. A defect that fires only inside a narrow disagreement window will be blamed on the operator every time, because the operator is the only visible actor. That is the reason it went unfound behind so many green `ac satisfy` calls.

## What this does NOT establish

The exact intra-window ordering is INFERRED, not instrumented. I did not `jq` the disk extract during Run 1, so I did not directly observe the run-1 disk state; that it was unsatisfied is read off the committed `5deb477c`. Whether the extract was unsatisfied at commit because `ac satisfy`'s regeneration had not flushed, or because the watcher ingested a pre-regeneration snapshot and rewrote it, is not pinned. The observable facts are: the store read 5/9 live, the committed extract read unsatisfied, and disk==store prevented recurrence. A fuller proof would log the watcher's ingest events against the satisfy write and show the reversion write with no client; not done.
